rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing assertion confirms that God truly imposed these prohibitions on the Jews and refutes their denial that they were divine punishment.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { وإنا لصادقون } تذييل للجملة التي قبلها قصدا لتحقيق أن الله حرم عليهم ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews wrongly attributed these restrictions to Jacob: he only forbade himself camel meat and milk, and a personal vow or bodily benefit did not bind his descendants.
rows.anchor: وليس قولهم بحق : لأن يعقوب إنما حرم على نفسه لحوم الإبل وألبانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur links the emphatic rebuttal to the challenge in 3:93–95: the prohibitions were written in the Torah, so the Jews could not deny them.
rows.anchor: وأن هذه الأشياء التي ذكر الله تحريمها على بني إسرائيل مذكور تحريمها في التوراة فكيف ينكرون تحريمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about having a settled place on earth is coordinated with the preceding clause that some are enemies to others.
rows.anchor: وعطفت جملة : { ولكم في الأرض مستقر } على جملة : { بعضكم لبعض عدو }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مستقر is a mimetic verbal noun meaning remaining or staying; Ibn Ashur points to the same word in two other verses.
rows.anchor: والمستقر مصدر ميمي والاستقرار هو المكث وقد تقدم القول فيه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes took the settled place to mean burial, but Ibn Ashur rejects this because enjoyment is mentioned and jinn and devils are not buried in the earth.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد به الدفن كما فسر به بعض المفسرين لأن قوله ومتاع يصد عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: متاع and تمتع mean gaining nonlasting pleasures and desires; متاع can also denote the things from which one benefits.
rows.anchor: والمتاع والتمتع : نيل الملذات والمرغوبات غير الدائمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حين means a period, long or short; it is indefinite here because its duration varies among kinds and individuals.
rows.anchor: والحين المدة من الزمن ، طويلة أو قصيرة ، وقد نكر هنا ولم يحدد لاختلاف مقداره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The period is the life in which a being can perceive pleasures and persist as a living self; this divinely determined term ends with life, ending settled existence and enjoyment, and is neither favor nor punishment.
rows.anchor: وهذا الزمن المقارن لحالة الحياة والإدراك هو المسمى بالأجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating قال without a conjunction departs from the expected coordination, although the speaker and general purpose are the same.
rows.anchor: والغرضض متحدا ، خروجا عن مقتضى الظاهر لأن مقتضى الظاهر في مثله هو العطف

rows.speaker: جمهور الحذاق من المفسرين
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur says most leading commentators did not explain the lack of coordination, perhaps treating it as a storytelling convention; al-Zamakhshari is among them.
rows.anchor: وقد أهمل توجيه ترك العطف جمهور الحذاق من المفسرين : الزمخشري وغيره ، ولعله رأى ذلك أسلوبا من أساليب الحكاية

rows.speaker: ابن عرفة التونسي
rows.claim: Ibn Arafa explains the analogous repeated قال at 7:140 by a change in discourse: the first statement rejects idolatry itself, the second argues against it; al-Khafaji also gives this explanation without attribution.
rows.anchor: هو الشيخ محمد بن عرفة التونسي في ( املاءات التفسير ) المروية عنه ، فإنه قال في قوله تعالى الآتي في هذه السورة

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: Abu al-Su'ud offers as one explanation that repeating قال emphasizes the statement that they will live on earth.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو السعود : إعادة القول إما لإظهار الاعتناء بمضمون ما بعده ، وهو قوله : { فيها تحيون }

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: Abu al-Su'ud also suggests omitted intervening speech, comparing 15:56–57 and 17:61–62; Ibn Ashur rejects this because reported speech need not be exhaustive or continuous.
rows.anchor: والتوجيه الثاني مردود إذ لا يلزم في حكاية الأقوال الإحاطة ولا الاتصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense of tribulation is testing; when attributed to God it is a rational metaphor meaning that He tests people’s adherence to religious laws.
rows.anchor: وأصل البلوى الاختبار ، والبلوى إذا أسندت إلى الله تعالى كانت مجازا عقليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The باء is causal and ما is a verbal noun: their deep immersion in disobedience made them rush into more sin whenever its impulse arose, disregarding God’s command.
rows.anchor: والباء للسببية و ( ما ) مصدرية ، أي بفسقهم ، أي توغلهم في العصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This إذ-clause coordinates with the earlier إذ يعدون; it means “ask them about the time a group said,” with إذ a past-time noun rather than an adverb.
rows.anchor: جملة : { وإذ قالت أمة منهم } عطف على قوله : { إذ يعدون } ( الأعراف : 163 ) والتقدير : واسأل بني إسرائيل إذ قالت أمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers back to the people whom the Prophet is told to ask, not to the town, since the passage rebukes all the Israelites.
rows.anchor: والضمير المجرور بمن عائد إلى ما عاد إليه ضمير { أسألهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the dialogue occurred in that town, its location is incidental: the story displays another instance of Israelite defiance and the poor effect of admonition, known among their scholars and righteous people.
rows.anchor: بل منظورا إليه بأنه مظهر آخر من مظاهر عصيانهم وعتوهم وقلة جدوى الموعظة فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here umma means a group sharing this statement; commentators describe three groups: persistent admonishers, admonishers who despaired, and people persisting in wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: والأمة الجماعة من الناس المشتركة في هذا القول ، قال المفسرون : إن أمة من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse abbreviates the groups’ prior history: the question shows they had objected after seeing admonition fail, while 7:165 identifies the warners as the rescued group and the wrongdoers as the punished group.
rows.anchor: وقد أجملت الآية ما كان من الأمة القائلة إيجازا في الكلام ، اعتمادا على القرينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur connects the term for admonition to its earlier uses at 4:63 and 7:145.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم ذكر الوعظ عند قوله تعالى : { فأعرض عنهم وعظهم في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The لام asks for a reason; the question is censuring and effectively denies any reason to admonish when the addressees believe no one can be brought to heed.
rows.anchor: واللام في لم تعظون } للتعليم ، فالمستفهم عنه من نوع العلل ، والاستفهام إنكاري في معنى النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people addressed by تعظون are a different group from the group asking why they admonish.
rows.anchor: والمخاطب ب { تعظون } أمة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The active participles refer to the future; their alternative wording shows that one of two punishments is certain, while which one remains undetermined.
rows.anchor: واسما الفاعل في قوله : { مهلكهم أو معذبهم } مستعملان في معنى الاستقبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer is set off as a separate sentence because it occurs within a dialogue.
rows.anchor: وفصلت جملة { قالوا } لوقوعها في سياق المحاورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: معذرة is an irregular mimetic verbal noun from اعتذر, meaning to present an excuse; an excuse is a reason or proof offered to remove blame, and اعتذار takes إلى in the sense of conveying it to someone.
rows.anchor: والمعذرة بفتح الميم وكسر الذال مصدر ميمي لفعل ( اعتذر ) على غير قياس

rows.speaker: الجمهور وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Most readers read معذرة in the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject (“our admonition is an excuse”); Hafs from Asim reads it accusative of purpose (“we admonish to excuse ourselves”).
rows.anchor: وبالرفع قرأه الجمهور ، وقرأه حفص عن عاصم بالنصب على المفعول لأجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hope that they may become God-fearing is a second reason to persist in admonition, since repetition may affect them.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { ولعلهم يتقون } علة ثانية للاستمرار على الموعظة أي رجاء لتأثير الموعظة فيهم بتكرارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One righteous group despaired of admonition and expected punishment; another still hoped repetition might work, so it continued to preach as a precaution and excuse before God.
rows.anchor: فالفريق الأول أخذوا بالطرف الراجح الموجب للظن . والفريق الثاني أخذوا بالطرف المرجوح جمعا بينه وبين الراجح لقصد الاحتياط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “they forgot” refers to the offending people; forgetting is figurative for turning away in a way that leads to forgetting.
rows.anchor: وضمير { نسوا } عائد إلى { قوما } والنسيان مستعمل في الإعراض المفضي إلى النسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who forbid evil are both admonishing groups mentioned in the preceding verse; the wrongdoers are the group whose destruction the questioners expected.
rows.anchor: والذين ينهون عن السوء } هم الفريقان المذكوران في قوله آنفا { وإذ قالت أمة منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoing here means disobedience that wrongs the self by failing to fulfill God’s right through obedience.
rows.anchor: والظلم هنا بمعنى العصيان ، وهو ظلم النفس ، حق الله تعالى في عدم الامتثال لأمره

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Nafi and Abu Ja'far read بيس with a kasra on bā, a long yā, and tanwin, from بئس with the hamza softened to yā, like ذيب from ذئب.
rows.anchor: قرأه نافع وأبو جعفر بكسر الباء الموحدة مشبعة بياء تحتية ساكنة وبتنوين السين

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads بئس with a still hamza and tanwin, deriving it from بئيس.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ابن عامر { بئس } بالهمزة الساكنة وإبقاء التنوين على أن أصله بئيس

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read بئيس with open bā, kasra on hamza, a still yā, and tanwin; it is either an intensive adjective from misery or a verbal noun like عذير and نكير.
rows.anchor: وقرأه الجمهور { بئيس } بفتح الموحدة وهمزة مكسورة بعدها تحتية ساكنة وتنوين السين

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Abu Bakr from Asim reads بيئس on the pattern صيقل, an intensive name for one characterized by hardship.
rows.anchor: وقرأه أبو بكر عن عاصم { بيئس } بوزن صيقل ، على أنه اسم للموصوف بفعل البؤس مبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All these readings convey a torment causing severe harm.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ، على جميع القراءات : أنه عذاب شديد الضر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view makes the severe torment a punishment before metamorphosis: the people who ignored admonition first suffer hardship, then witnesses who persist in defiance suffer the harsher transformation.
rows.anchor: فقيل هو عذاب غير المسخ المذكور بعده ، وهو عذاب أصيب به الذين نسوا ما ذكروا به

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A second view identifies the severe torment with metamorphosis itself; 7:166 then explains it, while restating the people's forgetfulness and defiance to stress their concurrence.
rows.anchor: وقيل : العذاب البئس هو المسخ ، فيكون قوله : { فلما عتوا عما نهوا عنه } بيانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The admonition they forgot and the prohibition they transgressed refer to the same thing; the expanded phrasing heightens the punishment and multiplies its forms instead of repeating words.
rows.anchor: و { ما ذكروا به } و { ما نهوا عنه } ما صدقهما شيء واحد ، فكان مقتضى الظاهر أن يقال

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur compares the verse’s amplification to Labid’s repeated simile, but judges the Qur'anic wording more eloquent and more beneficial.
rows.anchor: وهذا كإعادة التشبيه في قول لبيد : فتنازعا سبطا يطير ظلاله كدخان مشعلة يشب ضرامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلف is a verbal noun used for an agent, meaning someone who succeeds or differs; its image comes from what is behind rather than in front.
rows.anchor: وهو مصدر أريد به اسم الفاعل أي خالف ، والخلف مأخوذ من الخلف ضد القدام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successor group is not limited to one generation or century; context can make it extend through descendants, as in the later successors described at 19:59.
rows.anchor: ولا حد لآخر الخلف ، بل يكون تحديده بالقرائن ، فلا ينحصر في جيل ولا في قرن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Inherited” is metaphorical for taking another’s place; the phrase means succeeding others in possession of Scripture, a reading that works whichever group is meant.
rows.anchor: و { ورثوا } مجاز في القيام مقام الغير كما تقدم في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taking clause is circumstantial and condemns the successors; mentioning that they inherited Scripture first shows their misconduct was knowing and therefore worse.
rows.anchor: ومهد لذلك بأنهم ورثوا الكتاب ليدل على أنهم يفعلون ذلك عن علم لا عن جهل ، وذلك أشد مذمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking may be metaphorical for becoming involved in wrongdoing or literal for taking a thing into one’s possession.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الأخذ هنا الملابسة والاستعمال فهو مجاز أي : يلابسونه ، ويجوز كونه حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With both first vowels open, عرض means something transient and impermanent; it can refer to wealth or to available desires and benefits.
rows.anchor: والعرض بفتح العين وفتح الراء الأمر الذي يزول ولا يدوم . ويراد به المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الأدنى literally means nearer in place but here means worldly life; the demonstrative hints at contempt for the gain, as in Qays ibn al-Khatim’s verse.
rows.anchor: والأدنى الأقرب من المكان ، والمراد به هنا الدنيا ، وفي اسم الإشارة إيماء إلى تحقير هذا العرض

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وقتادة والطبري
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Tabari take the worldly gain as involvement in sins broadly, with taking used metaphorically for any manner of indulging in sin.
rows.anchor: وبذلك فسر سعيد بن جبير ، ومجاهد ، وقتادة ، والطبري ، فيشمل كل ذنب

rows.speaker: السدي ومعظم المفسرين
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and most commentators understand the gain as bribes and “taking” literally; Ibn Ashur says this better fits the next clause about similar gain coming to them.
rows.anchor: وقيل عرض الدنيا هو الرشا وبه فسرالسدي ، ومعظم المفسرين ، فيكون الأخذ مستعملا في حقيقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim may be spoken to people reproaching their sins, or may be inward self-talk that reassures them when a sense of restraint arises.
rows.anchor: والقول في : { ويقولون } هو الكلام اللساني ، يقولون لمن ينكر عليهم ملابسة الذنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive leaves God implicit as the known agent and generalizes the claim; the omitted object means “that” or “our sins.”
rows.anchor: وبناء فعل ( يغفر ) على صيغة المجهول لأن الفاعل معروف ، وهو الله ، إذ لا يصدر هذا الفعل إلا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They presumptuously expect all their sins to be forgiven without repentance, as in their claim that the Fire would touch them only for a few days.
rows.anchor: لأنهم يحسبون أن ذنوبهم كلها مغفورة { وقالوا لن تمسنا النار إلا أياما معدودة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لنا cannot be the passive subject: غفر takes one direct object, while the lām phrase expresses cause; compare شرح لك in 94:1, where لك could not become the نائب الفاعل either.
rows.anchor: وقوله { لنا } لا يصلح للنيابة عن الفاعل ، لأنه ليس في معنى المفعول ، إذ فعل المغفرة يتعدى لمفعول واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim of forgiveness is coordinated with their taking because both reports condemn them, and their combination intensifies the blame.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { ويقولون سيغفر لنا } معطوفة على جملة ، { يأخذون } لأن كلا الخبرين يوجب الذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If عرض means money, its coming pictures an offer; if it means forbidden pleasures, its coming pictures the desire arising in them, though “coming” better suits concrete things.
rows.anchor: واستعير إتيان العرض لبذله لهم إن كان المراد بالعرض المال ، وقد يراد به خطور شهوته في نفوسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They sin, assert their sins are forgiven, and continue sinning rather than desist.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أنهم يعصون ، ويزعمون أن سيئاتهم مغفورة ، ولا يقلعون عن المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question refutes their assertion by exposing its implication that God promised forgiveness; it is an aside addressed to the Prophet to use in argument against them.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { ألم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب } جواب عن قولهم : { سيغفر لنا } إبطالا لمضمونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative demands acknowledgment in order to rebuke them, since their own Scripture makes the covenant explicit.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام للتقرير المقصود منه التوبيخ ، وهذا التقرير لا يسعهم إلا الاعتراف به

words: أَن لَّا يَقُولُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْحَقَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah forbids adding to or subtracting from God's commands; it teaches repentance, not unearned forgiveness, so their claim falsely attributes a promise to God.
rows.anchor: ولا يجدون في الكتاب أنهم يغفر لهم ، وإنما يجدون فيه التوبة كما في الإصحاح من سفر التثنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant is Moses’ testament, which he conveyed from God in many places; the Book is the Torah of Moses.
rows.anchor: والميثاق : العهد ، وهو وصية موسى التي بلغها إليهم عن الله تعالى في مواضع كثيرة

words: أَن لَّا يَقُولُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْحَقَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive in “covenant of the Book” can mean a covenant within the Book or one known through it; أن may follow an omitted باء or explain the covenant in apposition.
rows.anchor: وإضافة الميثاق إلى الكتاب على معنى ( في ) أو على معنى اللام أي الميثاق المعروف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: درسوا coordinates with يؤخذ, which has past force after لم; the implied sense is “was not a covenant taken and did they not study,” asserting their study rather than merely reporting it.
rows.anchor: وفعل { درسوا } عطف على { يؤخذ } ، . لأن يؤخذ في معنى المضي ، لأجل دخول لم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant and their study of the Book together establish the charge against them, since they knew what they had promised not to say about God.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أنهم قد أخذ عليهم الميثاق بأن لا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق ، وهم عالمون بذلك الميثاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause is circumstantial: they knowingly violate Scripture while the afterlife is better than immediate gain, showing their choice was deliberate rather than careless.
rows.anchor: وفي جعل الجملة في موضع الحال تعريض بأنهم يعلمون ذلك أيضا فهم قد خيروا عليه عرض الدنيا قصدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reproach follows from the superiority of the afterlife; their preference for worldly gain treats them as irrational.
rows.anchor: وقرينة ذلك قوله : { أفلا تعقلون } المتفرع على قوله : { والدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون }

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وابن ذكوان وحفص عن عاصم ويعقوب وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Nafi, Ibn Amir, Ibn Dhakwan, Hafs from Asim, Yaqub, and Abu Ja'far read the verb with second-person tā’, shifting from narration to direct reproach; the remaining readers use third-person yā’ for indirect rebuke.
rows.anchor: وقد قريء بتاء الخطاب ، على الإلتفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب . ليكون أوقع في توجبه التوبيخ إليهم مواجهة ، وهي قراءة نافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the afterlife better implies that the offenders lost its good by taking worldly gain, and calling it better for the God-fearing implies the gain-takers are not pious; the phrase compresses these meanings with miraculous eloquence.
rows.anchor: وهذه معان كثيرة جمعها قوله : { والدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون أفلا تعقلون } وهذا من حد الإعجاز العجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse follows as a contrast: after condemning those who abandoned the covenant, it promises reward to those who uphold Scripture and its prophetic message.
rows.anchor: ووقعت جملة : { والذين يمسكون بالكتاب } إلى آخرها عقب التي قبلها : لأن مضمونها مقابل حكم التي قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing prayer is a metonym for accepting Muhammad, since prayer marks Islam and Muslims are called the people of the qibla; Ibn Ashur identifies these people as Jews awaiting and then believing the foretold final messenger, such as Abdullah ibn Salam.
rows.anchor: فكني عن الإيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بإقامة الصلاة ، لأن الصلاة شعار دين الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur also allows that the verse addresses Muslims, praising them as successful in the afterlife and assuring them they will not treat their Scripture as the Jews treated theirs.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن المراد بالذين يمسكون بالكتاب : المسلمون ، ثناء عليهم بأنهم الفائزون في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final sentence reports God's promise to those who hold fast; they are the reformers, left implicit because the description already includes them and the omission gives concise praise.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { إنا لا نضيع أجر المصلحين } خبر عن الذين يمسكون ، والمصلحون هم
